title: Define Ready-marking SLA in control plane + gate routing on Ready capacity only
creator: Lauren Bishop
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
body:
Context
Dedicated capacity bring-up is moving to an automated provision→ready pipeline. We need unambiguous semantics for when a pool is considered usable (“Ready”), an SLA for how quickly the control plane reflects that readiness, and a hard gating rule so routing never serves traffic from non-Ready capacity.

This ticket covers:
1) Document the Ready SLA + semantics (control plane state machine behavior; what inputs are required to mark Ready).
2) Implement routing gating: only advertise / route to pools marked Ready.
3) Add safety + observability: metrics and guardrails to ensure we detect regressions (e.g., Ready set too early).

Problem / pain
- Prior behavior was inconsistent across regions/pools: some pools were effectively usable while still “Validating”, and some were marked “Ready” before perf-canary completed.
- During pilot, routing briefly sent traffic to a pool that was still running validation smoke tests, causing intermittent 5xx. We mitigated by manually keeping the pool out of routing, but the system should enforce this.

Definitions
- Provisioned: infra exists and nodes are reachable; does NOT imply runtime is healthy or registered.
- Validating: readiness gates in progress (GPU health, networking/TLS/DNS, runtime smoke test) + perf-canary readiness suite.
- Ready: all validation gates have passed AND the control plane has successfully persisted Ready with an associated provenance record (run id + versions).

Ready MUST mean:
- Nodes pass GPU health checks (incl. ECC thresholds) and kube node readiness is stable for N minutes.
- Runtime components installed at pinned versions (chart/runtime version recorded).
- Networking checks pass (cluster DNS, outbound allowlist, TLS to control plane endpoints, registry/artifact access).
- Runtime smoke test passes for configured model(s) OR “generic” runtime health endpoints when model isn’t preloaded.
- Perf-canary readiness suite passes within pool/SKU/region-specific thresholds.
- Control plane registration complete and heartbeats observed.

SLA (Control Plane Ready Marking)
We are formalizing two related SLAs:

A) Ready-mark propagation SLA (internal platform)
- Once the provisioning workflow emits “validation_passed” for a pool run, the control plane must mark the pool Ready within:
  - p50: 2 minutes
  - p95: 10 minutes
- Excludes periods where provisioning is paused or in manual override.
- Measured via provisioning run correlation_id from “validation_passed” event → “pool_state=Ready persisted” event.

B) Routing safety SLA (customer-impacting)
- Routing must not advertise or route traffic to pools unless pool_state == Ready.
- Target: 0 requests served from non-Ready pools (hard invariant).
- If control plane state is unknown/unavailable: routing fails closed for NEW pools (do not add capacity), but does not drop existing Ready pools.

Implementation plan
1) Control plane contract
- Add/confirm a single source-of-truth field pool_state with enum: Requested/Provisioning/Imaging/Bootstrapping/Validating/Ready/Failed.
- Ready persistence is transactional with associated validation proof:
  - provisioning_run_id
  - perf_canary_summary_hash (or link)
  - versions: runtime, helm chart, golden image
  - timestamps: validation_start/end, ready_marked_at
- Ensure Ready is only set after perf-canary completion and validation gates (guard against race).

2) Routing integration
- Update pool discovery/advertisement logic to filter strictly on pool_state == Ready.
- Explicitly treat Validating as NOT usable.
- Add metric: routing.filtered_pools_total{reason="not_ready"}
- Add safe fallback: if a pool flips from Ready→non-Ready (future drift detection), remove from advertisement but keep existing in-flight requests unaffected.

3) Observability
- Emit events for:
  - ready_mark_attempted
  - ready_mark_succeeded
  - ready_mark_failed (with reason)
- Metrics:
  - time_to_ready_mark_seconds (validation_passed→ready_mark_succeeded)
  - non_ready_pool_advertisement_attempts_total (should be 0)
  - routing_requests_by_pool_state (guardrail; should be 0 for non-Ready)

4) Documentation
- Confluence: “Ready semantics and SLA” section added to Provision-to-ready overview and linked from routing runbook.
- Operator note: If validation is complete but Ready is not set within 10 minutes, treat as control-plane issue; see troubleshooting steps.

Acceptance criteria
- Routing does not route to pools in Provisioning/Imaging/Bootstrapping/Validating.
- Automated tests cover:
  - pool in Validating is excluded from routing
  - pool transitions to Ready enables routing
  - regression test for race: Ready cannot be set before perf-canary completion
- Dashboard panels exist for:
  - Ready-mark propagation p50/p95
  - Non-Ready routing guardrail (must stay at 0)
- Written SLA and semantics reviewed by Platform + SRE + Dedicated PM.

Links
- Confluence: Provision-to-ready automation overview (Ready vs Provisioned definitions)
- Confluence: Dedicated capacity readiness SLO (ties to overall time-to-ready)
- PR (routing gating): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48234
- PR (race fix): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48245

Open questions
- Do we ever want an intermediate “ReadyNoTraffic” state for warmup? Decision: not in this sprint; use pool_state=Validating until it’s safe to serve.
- Should we page on Ready-mark propagation p95 > 10m? SRE leaning: page only if impact is blocking customer expansion; otherwise create ticket + Slack notification. Follow-up tracked in ENG-2749/alerts.
comments: 2025-02-22 (Ravi Menon): Drafted Ready semantics + proposed SLA numbers (p50 2m / p95 10m). Main goal is hard invariant: routing never serves from non-Ready. Syncing with Mina/Ethan on where best to enforce filtering (routing service vs upstream pool registry query).

2025-02-26 (Ethan Park): +1 on filtering at routing boundary even if control plane query already filters. Defense-in-depth. Also suggest storing provisioning_run_id + versions on Ready to make audits easier.

2025-03-01 (Rafael Mendes): SRE request: add a guardrail metric that explicitly counts any request served where pool_state!=Ready (should be 0). This helps catch backdoor paths or cached advertisements. Also document failure mode: control plane state unknown should fail closed for new pools.

2025-03-05 (Ravi Menon): Implemented routing gating PR #48234. Adds filtering + metrics; unit tests added. Remaining: handle race where Ready set before perf-canary completes (saw once in staging). Creating small follow-up patch with Mina.

2025-03-08 (Mina Haddad): Found real race: perf-canary event arriving after validation summary due to async queue ordering. Need to make Ready set conditional on perf-canary completion record in same transaction. Patch in flight.
2025-03-10 (Ravi Menon): Race fix merged in PR #48245. Added regression test that forces event reorder and asserts Ready not set early.

2025-03-14 (Lauren Bishop): Product sign-off: Ready definition aligns with what we can message to Sales/CS (“Ready means safe to route traffic; validation and perf checks complete”). Please link to troubleshooting doc for cases where infra is up but not Ready.
2025-03-18 (Aisha Bello): Dashboard panel added for ready_mark propagation; p95 target annotated at 10m. We’re good on metrics naming; wiring into dedicated readiness dashboard spec.

2025-03-20 (Ravi Menon): Marking Done. Routing now only uses Ready capacity; guardrail metrics in place. Confluence updates linked. Any alerting/paging policy changes tracked under ENG-2749 + SRE alerts doc.
